goal: Measure how graph-width structure, variable order, and compilation schedule affect exact ROBDD compilation of the positive monotone 2-CNF F_G = AND_{(u,v) in E}(x_u OR x_v), which embeds directly into the boundary-CNF certifier family. Distinguish final representation size from intermediate compilation blowup and preserve exact cardinality-by-rank counts.

implementation.manager: fresh pure-Python reduced ordered BDD manager per cell with arbitrary fixed order encoded by relabeling variables to order positions
implementation.rank_count: exact cardinality polynomial by recursive branch convolution, counting satisfying assignments by Hamming weight
implementation.vertex_separation: for a vertex order, max over prefixes of the number of prefix vertices having at least one neighbor in the suffix
implementation.greedy_order: append the not-yet-placed vertex that minimizes the resulting current frontier size, breaking ties by degree then vertex id
implementation.balanced_pairwise: build each clause BDD, then repeatedly AND adjacent pairs in a balanced binary tree; no clause-at-a-time persistent core
implementation.dynamic_reordering_scope: No claim of reproducing CUDD sifting/window/group-sifting. The experiment is fixed-order plus schedule pathology only; CUDD heuristics remain an external implementation frontier.

required: Within each graph family, all variable orders and compilation schedules must yield exactly the same rank-count vector.

For every cell, evaluate the final BDD on 1024 deterministic pseudorandom assignments and require exact equality with direct CNF evaluation; if 2^n <= 262144 also exhaustively evaluate all assignments.
correctness.failure_policy: Any mismatch is a correctness failure; do not interpret timing or size comparisons from a failed cell.

resource_guard.on_guard: mark guarded_out, retain partial exact measurements, and do not infer a lower bound from timeout/guard alone

preregistered_interpretation: Path/tree cells are low-width controls; grid and random cubic cells probe higher pathwidth/order sensitivity.
A strong correlation between vertex-separation width and final OBDD nodes is descriptive support for width-aware switching, not a new asymptotic theorem.
If balanced compilation reduces allocated/intermediate work while final reachable nodes stay identical, that isolates compilation-order blowup from final OBDD lower bounds.

If every tested order remains large on random cubic cells, label only these concrete instances hard under tested orders; do not claim expander certification or all-order hardness from the experiment alone.
Exact rank counts, not total model count alone, are the required downstream query capability.
external_scope_anchors: Amarilli, Monet, Senellart: constant-arity/degree monotone CNFs have OBDD size exponential in pathwidth in the stated theorem scope.
Bova, Slivovsky: bounded-degree expander-based CNF families give exponential OBDD lower bounds.
De Colnet SAT 2023: clause-at-a-time incremental bottom-up compilation can have exponential intermediate blowup even where another bottom-up schedule is polynomial.
CUDD supports dynamic reordering including sifting, symmetric/group sifting, window permutation, annealing, genetic, and exact methods; these are not reproduced by this v0 runner.
decision_rule: Use results to decide whether the next implementation experiment should prioritize variable-order search, compilation-schedule rebuild triggers, or alternative structured representations. No result here authorizes lemma-library promotion/demotion or relaxes any safety/evidence gate.
